key_insight: C^2MF models per-instance, context-specific source credibility using conditional probabilistic circuits, allowing the fusion process to dynamically reweight modalities and resolve conflicts when sensors or modalities become unreliable.
problem_solved: Overcomes static, global assumptions about modality reliability by detecting and adapting to instance- and context-dependent modality corruption (e.g., sensor degradation or class-specific noise) during multimodal fusion.
method: Estimate per-instance credibility for each modality conditioned on context (input features, class, environment) so reliability is dynamic rather than fixed.
Use conditional probabilistic circuits to represent joint distributions and perform tractable, uncertainty-aware inference that weights modality contributions according to estimated credibility.
Train the system end-to-end (or with latent reliability estimation) to calibrate credibility scores and produce robust fused predictions under sensor/class-specific corruptions.
impact: Enables practitioners to build multimodal systems that are more robust and interpretable under real-world reliability shifts, improving performance and safety when sensors fail or data are corrupted.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: multiple modality inputs → per-instance credibility estimator → conditional probabilistic circuit fusion → final prediction (showing dynamic weights)
Credibility heatmap: per-sample or per-class modality reliability visualization highlighting when a modality is downweighted
Comparison chart: accuracy/robustness under different corruption scenarios contrasting C^2MF vs static-fusion baselines
Schematic of a probabilistic circuit: nodes showing conditioning and efficient tractable inference for clarity
paper_title: Context-specific Credibility-aware Multimodal Fusion with Conditional Probabilistic Circuits
paper_authors: Pranuthi Tenali, Sahil Sidheekh, Saurabh Mathur, Erik Blasch, Kristian Kersting
